title: Layered latent-state formalization and nonlinear star-system architecture
research_question: How can source-language Zhongzhou knowledge be represented without collapsing star properties, relational effects, palace context, valence and observable events into one label?
before_state: A flat star-to-event label system or simple additive score would conflate state properties with context-dependent outcomes and fail to represent source conditions and provenance.
result: The accepted project model separates source wording from normalization, latent-state change from valence, star cores from star-system interactions, palace projection from latent state, and natal structure from temporal inputs.
key_insights: The project uses a layered L0-L4 ontology as a revisable research representation.
Fourteen major-star cores are base states, not complete chart interpretations.
Sixty basic star systems allow interaction deltas, principal/multi-mode representations and context gates rather than simple vector addition.
Twelve palaces are local nodes within a global sparse relation graph.
The Paper 1 model prioritizes fixed natal essence plus exogenous temporal inputs and state-dependent response; full recursive dynamics and control claims remain future work.
negative_findings: A flat positive/negative score or fixed linear sum is not an adequate general representation under the current source-grounded design.
Candidate ontology dimensions and interaction functions remain revisable; architectural approval does not freeze every candidate dimension.

boundaries.source_status: The layered model is a research normalization constrained by source material; modern layer labels are not presented as classical wording.
boundaries.implementation_status: Architecture specified and partly represented in project artifacts; not equivalent to complete corpus closure.
boundaries.internal_fidelity: The event does not certify all rules or all textbook cases as validated.
boundaries.empirical_status: No external prediction evidence is established.

authority_notes: The event is a synthesis of accepted project architecture. The term 'canonical method boundary' refers to project design, not canonical Zhongzhou doctrine.
